unite_adi: UPPER SECONDARY-PREP YEAR-LEVEL: B1 - THEME 11: PERSONAL LIFE AND WELL-BEING

bolumler.ogrenmeKanitlari: PERFORMANCE ASSIGNMENT: Students write and design a school drama play on the the content of ''body parts, human illnesses and diseases, human well-being, human nature, well-being for the future'' and then they present it and perform it as a show in class by inviting other students as patients, doctors, and nurses. The assignment is evaluated by using a rubric scheme, a rating scale, and/or a marking scheme. Öğrenme-Öğretme Yaşantıları
bolumler.temelKabuller: This theme includes the concept of ''personal life and well-being with its components such as body parts, human illnesses and diseases, human well-being, human nature, well-being for the future'' and it is assumed that it could be present in almost all languages, with some exceptions. It is assumed that a student in the preparatory year of an upper secondary school may know what body parts, human illnesses and diseases, human well-being, human nature, well-being for the future mean in their own language as it is known that almost all people who start to learn a new language bring their pre-existing knowledge (in their own language) with them and transfer it to their new language learning context. However, they may not know how to say these things in another language if this has not yet been covered in their existing curriculum. Fortunately, this existing knowledge in their own language can help them recognise, understand, and learn them more easily in a foreign language, in this case English. As they are students in the preparatory year of an upper secondary school, they are expected to know some basic vocabulary about ''personal life and well-being'' in English from previous themes and/or years such as '' leg, shoulder, flu, stomachache, pain, stress and so on'' and also some structures such as ''What does s/he look like? S/he looks very nice, What is the matter with her? She has a stomachache. How does he feel? She seems to be bored.'' in English from the previous themes and/or years. These grammar items and vocabulary are revised during the ''Revision Programme'' at the beginning of the year and they can be used as a basis for learning the new vocabulary and grammatical items in the current theme, so that the new grammatical elements in the current theme can be learnt easily.
bolumler.onDegerlendirme: It is assumed that these students in the preparatory year of an upper secondary school are ready to learn the concept of body parts, human illnesses and diseases, human well-being, human nature, well-being for the future'' cognitively, affectively, and socially since it is appropriate to their age and language level. Therefore, a large picture could be provided for the students to remember and practise the items that they are related and previously learnt so that they can discuss the picture in pairs and write down what they remember. This session can help them revise all the related vocabulary and grammatical elements that they have already learnt from previous themes or from previous years as a preparatory practice. In this way, their performance can be evaluated in terms of how much they remember and how accurately they use these items to build their competence in the current theme. It can help the teacher decide what to emphasise, revise, and practise in order to facilitate the new vocabulary and grammatical items in the current theme. (Their performance can be evaluated by rubrics, a rating scale, and /or a marking scheme during these practices.)
bolumler.zenginlestirme: Objective: To give advice about health and well-being in English by using target vocabulary and target grammar to improve writing and speaking skills. Activity 1: Advice for Health and Well-Being The teacher writes detailed scenarios related to health and well-being (e.g., ''A friend has a swollen ankle and cannot walk properly'', ''Your sibling feels stressed and cannot sleep well'', ''A neighbour is feeling dizzy after a long hike'', ''Your classmate is anxious about an upcoming exam''.) on slips of paper and places them in a box. Each student draws a scenario from the box and writes advice using ''should'' and advanced vocabulary (e.g., ''If your friend is stressed, they should try relaxation techniques like deep breathing''). After writing, students pair up to role-play as a person seeking advice and an advisor (e.g., Student A: ''I feel anxious about my exam. What should I do?''. Student B: ''You should plan your study schedule and take regular breaks to stay calm''. Finally, each pair presents their scenario and advice to the class, receiving constructive feedback from the teacher and classmates on meaning, creativity, use of vocabulary, grammar accuracy, and fluency. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity. Objective: To give advice about health and well-being in English by using the target vocabulary for improving listening, writing, and speaking skills. Activity 2: Listening for Health and Well-Being Advice The teacher explains to the class that they will do a listening activity about health and well-being advice. During the first listening, students listen carefully to understand the main ideas (e.g., ''If you feel anxious, you should try writing a journal''.). After the first listening, the teacher gives each student a worksheet with simple visuals (e.g., a person sitting at a desk looking stressed, a glass of water, or someone exercising). The visuals do not include any text. During the second listening, students write the advice they hear under the correct visual. During the third listening, students check and correct their answers. Afterward, students share their answers with the class. The teacher gives constructive feedback by praising correct matches (e.g., ''Well done, you matched the advice perfectly!''). Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
bolumler.destekleme: Objective: To talk about illnesses and symptoms in English by using the target vocabulary through developing their writing and speaking skills. Activity 1: Choose the correct word The teacher provides a worksheet with pictures depicting various illness-related situations (e.g., a person sneezing, a swollen arm, a fainting person) and a word bank containing words such as allergic, faint, feverish, infected, itchy, severe, and swollen. Students examine the pictures and choose the correct word from the Word Bank to write under each image (e.g., for a picture of a swollen arm, write ''swollen''.). Once completed, the teacher points to each picture, asks, ''What is this?'' and prompts students to respond, e.g., ''This is swollen''. The teacher emphasises correct pronunciation and provides positive feedback and encouragement. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity. Objective: To give advice about health and well-being in English by using target vocabulary and target grammar through improving their writing and speaking skills. Activity 2: Fill in the blanks The teacher provides example sentences such as, ''If you have a headache, you should drink water'', and ''If you feel tired, you should sleep early''. Students then complete sentences like, ''If you have a fever, you should ____________'', and ''If you feel stressed, you should ____________''. Afterward, students share their answers with the class. The teacher listens carefully and provides positive feedback by highlighting correct usage (e.g., ''Great advice! That’s exactly what someone should do!'') and gently corrects any errors (e.g., ''Good try! Let’s say it this way: -You should rest in bed-''. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
